PAYROLL TAX WITHHOLDING REFERENCE GUIDE — TAX YEAR 2026

SOCIAL SECURITY TAX (OASDI)
The Social Security wage base limit for 2026 is $176,100. Wages paid above this amount in the calendar year are not subject to Social Security tax. The employee Social Security tax rate is 6.2 percent of taxable wages. The employer Social Security tax rate matches the employee rate at 6.2 percent of taxable wages.

MEDICARE TAX
There is no wage base limit for Medicare tax; all covered wages are taxable. The employee Medicare tax rate is 1.45 percent of all wages. The employer Medicare tax rate is 1.45 percent of all wages.

ADDITIONAL MEDICARE TAX
Employers must withhold an Additional Medicare Tax of 0.9 percent on wages paid to an employee in excess of $200,000 in a calendar year, regardless of filing status. For employees filing as married filing jointly, the Additional Medicare Tax threshold used for estimated tax purposes is $250,000. The Additional Medicare Tax has no employer-matching portion.

SUPPLEMENTAL WAGES
When supplemental wages such as bonuses and commissions are paid separately from regular wages and total $1,000,000 or less for the year, employers may withhold at a flat supplemental wage rate of 22.0 percent. When an employee's cumulative supplemental wages during the calendar year exceed $1,000,000, the mandatory flat rate on the amount over $1,000,000 rises to 37.0 percent.

FEDERAL UNEMPLOYMENT TAX (FUTA)
The standard FUTA tax rate is 6.0 percent of the first $7,000 paid to each employee during the calendar year, which is also the FUTA wage base limit. Employers who pay state unemployment taxes timely and in full are typically eligible for a FUTA credit of 5.4 percent, producing a net FUTA rate of 0.6 percent.

FUTA CREDIT REDUCTION STATES
California is designated as a FUTA credit reduction state for 2026, with an applicable credit reduction rate of 0.6 percent, meaning employers in California pay an effective net FUTA rate of 1.2 percent. New York is also designated as a FUTA credit reduction state for 2026, with an applicable credit reduction rate of 0.9 percent, producing an effective net FUTA rate of 1.5 percent for New York employers.

BACKUP WITHHOLDING
When backup withholding applies because a payee has failed to furnish a correct taxpayer identification number, the backup withholding rate is 24.0 percent of the reportable payment.
